definition_en: the amount of matter or people in a given space, or the strength of something mixed in liquid
core_image: 同样大的方格里，一边放了三颗豆，一边塞了三十颗
scene: 老师往两个同样大的盒子里装豆子，一个很快装满，另一个还空着大半。The density of the city makes land very expensive.
sceneCN: 这里 density 指「密度」（第 1 个义项：单位空间里所含的量）；句意是这座城市的密度让土地变得非常昂贵。

senses.title: Mass in a given space
senses.definition: the amount of matter in a given space
senses.definitionCN: 一定空间内所含物质的量
senses.example: Lead has a much higher density than wood.
senses.exampleCN: 铅的密度比木头高得多。
senses.why: Density answers one question: how much in how little room.
senses.whyCN: 密度只回答一个问题：多小的空间里装了多少。

senses.title: Crowding of people or traffic
senses.definition: the state of people or vehicles being crowded together
senses.definitionCN: 人或车辆拥挤在一起的状态
senses.example: The density of traffic slows every bus.
senses.exampleCN: 交通的密度让每辆公交都变慢。
senses.why: A street can be measured the way a block of metal is measured.
senses.whyCN: 街道也能像一块金属那样被量出疏密。

senses.title: Strength of a mixture
senses.definition: the strength of a substance mixed into a liquid
senses.definitionCN: 某物质在液体中的浓度
senses.example: They measured the density of salt in the water.
senses.exampleCN: 他们测量了水中盐的浓度。
senses.why: Salt leaves no shape, so only its density can be counted.
senses.whyCN: 盐没有形状，只能靠浓度来计数。

intro.en: Density is Latin densitas, the quality of being densus, thick or crowded, plus the noun ending -ity.
intro.cn: density 是拉丁语 densitas，表示 densus（浓密、拥挤）这种性质，后面带上名词词尾 -ity。

items.en: Densus described thick woods, heavy fog and packed ranks.
items.cn: densus 形容茂密的树林、浓重的雾与挤紧的队列。

items.en: Densitas named the quality itself rather than the thing.
items.cn: densitas 指这种性质本身，而不是那样东西。

items.en: Science gave density a number: mass divided by volume.
items.cn: 科学给了密度一个数字：质量除以体积。

items.en: Cities and crowds began to be described by density too.
items.cn: 城市与人群也开始用密度来描述。

items.en: It now measures matter, people and even traffic.
items.cn: 如今它既量物质，也量人，甚至量交通。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the dens- stem, and the meaning group gives three measures of how much is packed in.
note.cn: 形近组共用 dens- 词干，近义组则给出三种衡量「装了多少」的说法。

entries.definition: packed closely together
in a closely packed way
to make something smaller or thicker
the amount of a substance in a mixture
entries.definitionCN: 混合物中某物质的含量

entries.definition: the distance between two sides
the state of too many things in one place
entries.definitionCN: 太多东西挤在一处的状态

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with two boxes of beans and end with salt that disappears into water.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从两盒豆子开始，落到盐溶进水里看不见。

normal.en: Same box, more beans: that is density in one picture.
normal.cn: 一样的盒子，装进更多豆子，这就是密度。

normal.en: Density is a fraction: what you have over the room it takes.
normal.cn: 密度是一个分数：有多少东西，除以它占的空间。

normal.en: A crowded train and a heavy metal share the same word.
normal.cn: 拥挤的列车与沉重的金属共用一个词。

normal.en: Salt in water keeps its density but loses its shape.
normal.cn: 盐在水里保住了浓度，却丢了形状。

normal.en: Add -ity to dense and the quality becomes countable.
normal.cn: dense 后面加 -ity，性质就变得可以计数。

abstract.en: Picture a spoon that stands upright in thick honey.
abstract.cn: 想象一把勺子直立在浓稠的蜂蜜里。

abstract.en: Picture a square metre of ground with thirty people on it.
abstract.cn: 想象一平方米的地上站了三十个人。

abstract.en: Picture a glass of water turning faintly salty.
abstract.cn: 想象一杯水慢慢有了淡淡的咸味。

examples.en: Lead has a much higher density than wood.
examples.cn: 铅的密度比木头高得多。

examples.en: The density of traffic slows every bus.
examples.cn: 交通的密度让每辆公交都变慢。

examples.en: They measured the density of salt in the water.
examples.cn: 他们测量了水中盐的浓度。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 density 记成「凳子 city」：一座城里凳子的数量除以城的面积，就是密度。

root: 来自拉丁语 densitas，由 densus（浓密、拥挤）加名词词尾 -ity 构成。它先把「稠密」当成一种性质，十七世纪科学又把它变成可计算的量：质量除以体积；后来城市、人群与交通也用它来衡量。

sensesIntro.en: From beans in a box, to matter on a scale, to people in a street, to salt in water.
sensesIntro.cn: 从盒里的豆子，到秤上的物质，到街上的人，再到水里的盐。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the same box holds far more beans when they are packed tight.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一个盒子，豆子挤紧后能装下多得多。

branches.en: The first sense is a number for matter in a space.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是空间里物质含量的数字。

branches.en: The second sense applies the same number to people and vehicles.
branches.cn: 第二个义项把同一个数字用在人与车辆上。

branches.en: The third sense measures what has dissolved out of sight.
branches.cn: 第三个义项衡量溶进水里、看不见的东西。

branches.en: Metal and traffic are both judged by how much fits in one place.
branches.cn: 金属与交通，都按一处能装多少来评判。

branches.en: A crowded street and a strong solution are both thick with something.
branches.cn: 拥挤的街道与浓溶液，都因为某样东西太多而变稠。

intro.en: Density sits at the centre of a family that runs from the adjective dense to verbs of pressing and measuring.
intro.cn: density 位于一个家族的中心，从形容词 dense 一直连到表示压紧与测量的动词。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin densus, thick or crowded, with -ity naming the quality.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是拉丁语 densus（浓密、拥挤），-ity 把这种性质变成名词。

items.meaning: the amount packed into a space
items.example: They measured the density of the liquid.
items.exampleCN: 他们测量了这种液体的密度。

items.example: The fog grew dense near the river.
The denseness of the crowd slowed us.
items.exampleCN: 人群的稠密让我们走得很慢。

items.meaning: to press together or turn to liquid
items.example: Steam condenses on the cold glass.

items.meaning: the change from gas to liquid

items.example: The densitometer gave a clear reading.
items.exampleCN: 密度计给出了清楚的读数。

items.example: They densified the soil before building.
items.exampleCN: 他们建房前把土压得更实。

definition_en: a person whose job is to examine and treat teeth
core_image: 一个人戴上口罩，头灯亮起，手里的小钻发出细响
scene: 走廊里飘着消毒水味，护士叫到名字，孩子握紧了妈妈的手。The dentist asked him to open wide and stay still.
sceneCN: 这里 dentist 指「牙医」（第 1 个义项：检查并治疗牙齿的人）；句意是牙医让他张大嘴并保持不动。

senses.title: A doctor for teeth
senses.definition: a doctor who examines and repairs teeth
senses.definitionCN: 检查并修复牙齿的医生
senses.example: The dentist asked him to open wide and stay still.
senses.exampleCN: 牙医让他张大嘴并保持不动。
senses.why: A dentist is the person you sit still for.
senses.whyCN: 牙医就是那个你坐着不动给他看的人。

senses.title: The dentist's office
senses.definition: the place where a dentist works, often called the dentist's
senses.definitionCN: 牙医工作的地方，常简称为牙医诊所
senses.example: I spent the whole morning at the dentist.
senses.exampleCN: 我整个上午都待在牙医诊所。
senses.why: English often names a shop or clinic after the person who runs it.
senses.whyCN: 英语常按经营它的人来称呼店铺或诊所。

intro.en: Dentist came from French dentiste, which joined dent, a tooth, with -iste, a person who works with something.
intro.cn: dentist 来自法语 dentiste，由 dent（牙齿）与 -iste（从事某事的人）组成。

items.en: Dentiste joined dent, tooth, with -iste, a person who works with something.
items.cn: dentiste 由 dent（牙齿）与 -iste（从事某事的人）合成。

items.en: Dentiste separated the tooth specialist from the general doctor.
items.cn: dentiste 把牙齿专家从普通医生里分了出来。

items.en: English borrowed dentist as the trade of tooth care grew.
items.cn: 随着护牙行业发展，英语借来了 dentist。

items.en: Licences and schools turned dentist into a trained profession.
items.cn: 执照与学校让牙医成为受过训练的职业。

items.en: A dentist now checks, cleans, fills and straightens teeth.
items.cn: 如今的牙医检查、清洁、补牙与矫正牙齿。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the dent- root, and the meaning group names other people who work on the mouth.
note.cn: 形近组共用 dent- 词根，近义组则给出其他在口腔里工作的人。

entries.definition: relating to teeth
the work and study of treating teeth
entries.definitionCN: 治疗牙齿的工作与学问

entries.definition: a set of artificial teeth
a specialist who straightens teeth
a doctor who performs operations
a doctor of general medicine

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a paper bib tied around a neck and end with a small mirror lifted out.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从系在脖子上的纸围兜开始，落到一面被取出的小镜子。

normal.en: Dent- is tooth and -ist is person: the tooth person.
normal.cn: dent- 是牙，-ist 是人，合起来就是跟牙打交道的人。

normal.en: You do not chat while the dentist is working.
normal.cn: 牙医干活的时候，你没法聊天。

normal.en: A dentist counts teeth the way a teacher counts students.
normal.cn: 牙医数牙齿，就像老师数学生。

normal.en: The chair goes down, the light comes on, the world shrinks to one tooth.
normal.cn: 椅子放倒，灯亮起来，世界缩成一颗牙。

normal.en: Dentist and dental share one root and two jobs.
normal.cn: dentist 与 dental 共用一个词根，却分两份工作。

abstract.en: Picture a mask hiding all but a pair of eyes.
abstract.cn: 想象一只口罩遮住整张脸，只露出一双眼睛。

abstract.en: Picture a tray of small tools laid in a neat row.
abstract.cn: 想象一盘小工具摆得整整齐齐。

abstract.en: Picture a child gripping a parent's hand in a waiting room.
abstract.cn: 想象候诊室里，孩子紧紧抓着家长的手。

examples.en: The dentist asked him to open wide and stay still.
examples.cn: 牙医让他张大嘴并保持不动。

examples.en: I spent the whole morning at the dentist.
examples.cn: 我整个上午都待在牙医诊所。

examples.en: A good dentist explains what the drill will do.
examples.cn: 好牙医会解释钻头要做什么。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 dentist 记成「凳子上的齿科人」：dent 是牙，ist 是人，坐在那张凳子上替你治牙的人就是牙医。

root: 来自法语 dentiste，由 dent（牙齿）与 -iste（从事某事的人）组成。十八世纪牙科从普通医学里独立出来，这个词随职业一起进入英语；十九世纪执照与学校出现后，它专指受过训练的牙医。

sensesIntro.en: From the person holding the mirror to the room where the chair waits.
sensesIntro.cn: 从那个拿着小镜子的人，到那张椅子等着的房间。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a masked face under a bright lamp above an open mouth.
core.cn: 核心意象：亮灯之下，一张口罩遮住的脸俯向张开的嘴。

branches.en: The first sense is the person who does the looking and the fixing.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是那个负责查看与修补的人。

branches.en: The second sense is the room named after that person.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是以那个人命名的房间。

branches.en: A trade and its workplace often borrow a single name.
branches.cn: 一门手艺和它的场所，常常共用一个名字。

branches.en: The word points at a trained professional, not just anyone with a mirror.
branches.cn: 这个词指的是受过训练的专业人士，不是随便拿面镜子的人。

branches.en: Going to the dentist can mean the chair, the bill and the wait.
branches.cn: 去看牙医，可能意味着椅子、账单和等待。

intro.en: Dentist belongs to the tooth family and names the person at its centre.
intro.cn: dentist 属于牙齿家族，并给这个家族的中心人物命名。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin dens, tooth, with the stem dent- and the agent ending -ist.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是拉丁语 dens（牙齿），词干 dent- 后面加表示人的词尾 -ist。

items.meaning: the work and study of teeth
items.example: She studied dentistry for five years.
Dental care matters at every age.
items.exampleCN: 牙齿护理在每个年龄都重要。
这些病人在牙齿状况上相似。

items.example: He cleaned his denture each night.

items.meaning: the clinic where a dentist works
items.example: I left my bag at the dentist's.
items.exampleCN: 我把包落在牙医诊所了。

definition_en: to say that something is not true, or to refuse to give something to someone
core_image: 一个人把递到面前的文件推回去，摇了摇头
scene: 记者连问三次，发言人每次都把同一句话重复一遍，眼睛没有离开稿子。The company denied that it had broken the law.
sceneCN: 这里 deny 指「否认」（第 1 个义项：说某事不是真的）；句意是公司否认自己违反了法律。

senses.title: Say it is not true
senses.definition: to state that something is not true
senses.definitionCN: 声明某事不是真的
senses.example: The company denied that it had broken the law.
senses.exampleCN: 公司否认自己违反了法律。
senses.why: A denial pushes a claim back before it can settle.
senses.whyCN: 否认就是把说法在落定之前推回去。

senses.title: Refuse to give
senses.definition: to refuse to allow or give something
senses.definitionCN: 拒绝允许或给予某物
senses.example: He was denied entry to the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 他被拒绝进入大厅。
senses.why: To deny a thing is to shut a door and keep it shut.
senses.whyCN: 拒绝给予，就是关上一扇门并不再打开。

intro.en: Deny came through Old French denier from Latin denegare, where de- means fully and negare means to say no.
intro.cn: deny 经古法语 denier 来自拉丁语 denegare，其中 de- 表示完全，negare 表示说不。

items.en: Denegare joined de-, meaning fully, with negare, to say no.
items.cn: denegare 由 de-（完全）与 negare（说不）合成。

items.en: Writers used denegare for refusing a request or a faith.
items.cn: 作家用 denegare 表示拒绝请求或背弃信仰。

items.en: Denier refused, forbade or said a thing was untrue.
items.cn: denier 可以表示拒绝、禁止，或说某事不实。

items.en: English took deny for both refusing and declaring false.
items.cn: 英语借来 deny，同时表示拒绝与宣布为假。

items.en: Today a person can deny a fact or be denied a chance.
items.cn: 如今人可以否认一个事实，也可能被剥夺一个机会。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the deny stem, and the meaning group moves from refusing a request to rejecting a statement.
note.cn: 形近组共用 deny 词干，近义组则从拒绝请求走到否掉一个说法。

entries.definition: a statement that something is not true
able to be said not to be true
a person who says something is false
to say you will not do or give something
to refuse to accept something
to say the opposite of what was said

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a document pushed back across a table and end with a door that stays closed.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一份被推回桌对面的文件开始，落到一扇始终关着的门。

normal.en: A shaken head is the shortest denial.
normal.cn: 摇一下头，就是最短的否认。

normal.en: Deny has two hands: one pushes a claim away, one withholds a gift.
normal.cn: deny 有两只手：一只推开说法，一只扣住东西不给。

normal.en: To deny a child a story is to shut a small door.
normal.cn: 不给孩子讲一个故事，就是关上一扇小小的门。

normal.en: A firm denial is a wall built in one sentence.
normal.cn: 一句坚决的否认，就是一句话砌成的一堵墙。

normal.en: Deny and denial differ only in their ending.
normal.cn: deny 与 denial 只差一个词尾。

abstract.en: Picture a palm pressing a sheet of paper flat on a desk.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手掌把一张纸按平在桌上。

abstract.en: Picture a hand closing around a key and putting it away.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手攥住钥匙，把它收了起来。

abstract.en: Picture a doorway with a person standing in it, arms crossed.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人站在门口，双臂交叉。

examples.en: The company denied that it had broken the law.
examples.cn: 公司否认自己违反了法律。

examples.en: He was denied entry to the hall.
examples.cn: 他被拒绝进入大厅。

examples.en: There is no denying that the plan has failed.
examples.cn: 不可否认，这个计划已经失败。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 deny 记成「抵赖」：de 像「抵」，ny 像「赖」，把做过的事抵掉不认，就是否认。

root: 来自拉丁语 denegare，由 de-（完全）与 negare（说不）组成，经古法语 denier 进入英语。它先同时表示拒绝请求与宣布某事不实，后来两条线都保留下来：一条说「这不是真的」，一条说「这个不给你」。

sensesIntro.en: From pushing a claim back across the table to closing the door on a request.
sensesIntro.cn: 从把说法推回桌对面，到对请求关上大门。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sheet of paper pushed back and a head shaking once.
core.cn: 核心意象：一份文件被推回来，一颗头摇了一下。

branches.en: The first sense is a wall built against a statement.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是针对一个说法砌起的墙。

branches.en: The second sense is a closed hand, not an argument.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是一只攥紧的手，不是一场辩论。

branches.en: Both senses say no, one to a fact and one to a request.
branches.cn: 两个义项都在说不，一个对事实，一个对请求。

branches.en: In argument, deny means the other side has not proved its case.
branches.cn: 在争论里，deny 意味着对方没有证明自己的说法。

branches.en: In daily life, deny means a chance is taken away.
branches.cn: 在日常里，deny 意味着一个机会被拿走了。

intro.en: Deny grows a family of nouns and adjectives about saying no and about what cannot be said no to.
intro.cn: deny 长出一族名词与形容词，讲说不，也讲不容说不。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin negare, to say no, strengthened by de-.
latinIntro.cn: 它的词基是拉丁语 negare（说不），前面用 de- 加强。

items.meaning: to say no to a claim or a request
items.example: She denied the charge at once.

items.meaning: a statement that something is false
items.exampleCN: 他的否认没说服任何人。
这个说法几乎无法否认。

items.meaning: in a way that cannot be denied

items.exampleCN: 否认者重复了他的说法。
这张便条给了他推脱的余地。

items.meaning: in a way that can be denied
items.exampleCN: 这道命令含糊得可以否认。

definition_en: to leave a place, especially to begin a journey, or to turn away from what is usual
core_image: 站台上一个人的背影越来越小，列车把灯光拉成一条线
scene: 车门关上，站台上的人挥手，列车慢慢滑出灯光。The night train departs at ten.
sceneCN: 这里 depart 指「出发」（第 1 个义项：离开某地开始旅程）；句意是夜班列车十点出发。

senses.title: Leave to begin a journey
senses.definition: to leave a place in order to start a trip
senses.definitionCN: 离开某地以开始一段旅程
senses.example: The night train departs at ten.
senses.exampleCN: 夜班列车十点出发。
senses.why: A journey begins at the moment the place is left behind.
senses.whyCN: 旅程就在把地方留在身后的那一刻开始。

senses.title: Leave a place or a post
senses.definition: to go away from a place or a position
senses.definitionCN: 从某地或某个职位走开
senses.example: She departed without a word.
senses.exampleCN: 她一句话没说就离开了。
senses.why: Not every leaving is an adventure; some are just endings.
senses.whyCN: 不是每次离开都是远行，有些只是结束。

senses.title: Turn away from a rule
senses.definition: to stop following what is usual or expected
senses.definitionCN: 不再遵循通常或预期的做法
senses.example: The design departs from tradition.
senses.exampleCN: 这个设计背离了传统。
senses.why: A path that leaves the main road is also departing.
senses.whyCN: 离开大路的小径，也是一种 depart。

intro.en: Depart came through Old French departir from Latin departire, where de- means apart and partire means to divide.
intro.cn: depart 经古法语 departir 来自拉丁语 departire，其中 de- 表示分开，partire 表示划分。

items.en: Departire joined de-, meaning apart, with partire, to divide.
items.cn: departire 由 de-（分开）与 partire（划分）合成。

items.en: Departir meant to divide, to separate or to leave.
items.cn: departir 表示划分、分开或离开。

items.en: English took depart for separating and for going away.
items.cn: 英语借来 depart，既表示分开，也表示走开。

items.en: The sense of starting a journey settled in travel writing.
items.cn: 开始旅程这一层意思在游记里固定下来。

items.en: Now it also describes leaving a job or a tradition.
items.cn: 如今它也指离开一份工作或一种传统。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the depart stem, and the meaning group moves from simply leaving to setting off and pulling away.
note.cn: 形近组共用 depart 词干，近义组则从单纯离开走到动身与抽身。

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a closing carriage door and end with a path that leaves the main road.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从关上的车门开始，落到一条离开大路的小径。

normal.en: De- means apart, so depart is to part from a place.
normal.cn: de- 表示分开，depart 就是与一个地方分开。

normal.en: A train departs; a passenger is left holding a ticket.
normal.cn: 列车出发了，乘客手里只剩一张票。

normal.en: Leaving a job is also a departure, even without a train.
normal.cn: 辞掉一份工作也是离开，哪怕没有列车。

normal.en: A design can depart from tradition without going anywhere.
normal.cn: 一个设计可以背离传统，却哪儿也没去。

normal.en: Depart, departure and department all begin with the same parting.
normal.cn: depart、departure 与 department 都从同一个「分开」开始。

abstract.en: Picture a platform lamp stretching into a thin line.
abstract.cn: 想象站台的灯被拉成一条细线。

abstract.en: Picture a desk cleared of everything but a key.
abstract.cn: 想象一张桌子被清空，只剩一把钥匙。

abstract.en: Picture footprints turning off a wide road onto grass.
abstract.cn: 想象脚印从大路拐进草地。

examples.en: The night train departs at ten.
examples.cn: 夜班列车十点出发。

examples.en: She departed without a word.
examples.cn: 她一句话没说就离开了。

examples.en: The design departs from tradition.
examples.cn: 这个设计背离了传统。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 depart 记成「地跑」：de 像「地」，part 是分开，人从一块地上分开跑开，就是离开与出发。

root: 来自拉丁语 departire，由 de-（分开）与 partire（划分）组成，经古法语 departir 进入英语。它先表示分开与离开，十七世纪起在游记里固定为出发；现代又引申为离开职位、背离传统。

sensesIntro.en: From a train pulling out, to a person walking away, to a design leaving the old path.
sensesIntro.cn: 从开出的列车，到走开的人，再到离开旧路的设计。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a platform lamp stretches into a line as the train pulls out.
core.cn: 核心意象：列车开走时，站台的灯被拉成一条线。

branches.en: The first sense is a journey with a time on the board.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是牌子上写着时间的旅程。

branches.en: The second sense is a person simply not there any more.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是一个人不再出现在那里。

branches.en: The third sense is an idea stepping off the usual road.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是一个想法走下惯常的道路。

branches.en: A train and a worker can both leave on schedule.
branches.cn: 列车与工作者都能按时离开。

branches.en: Leaving a place and leaving a habit are both partings.
branches.cn: 离开一个地方与离开一种习惯，都是分别。

intro.en: Depart shares its root with departure and department, a family all about dividing and going apart.
intro.cn: depart 与 departure、department 共用词根，这一族词都关于划分与分开。

latinIntro.en: The base is partire, to divide, with de- meaning apart; the same root gives part and partial.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是 partire（划分），de- 表示分开；同一个词根还给出 part 与 partial。

senses.title: A division of an organization
senses.definition: one of the parts into which a large organization is divided
senses.definitionCN: 大机构被划分成的部分之一
senses.example: She works in the sales department of a small company.
senses.exampleCN: 她在小公司的销售部工作。
senses.why: When an organization grows past one table, it begins to cut itself into parts.
senses.whyCN: 当一个机构一张桌子坐不下，它就开始把自己切成几块。

senses.title: A subject area at a university
senses.definition: a group of teachers and courses in one subject
senses.definitionCN: 同一学科的老师与课程组成的单位
senses.example: She teaches in the history department.
senses.exampleCN: 她在历史系任教。
senses.why: A university is also too large for one voice, so it divides by subject.
senses.whyCN: 大学也大到容不下一个声音，于是按学科分开。

senses.title: A section of a large shop
senses.definition: one of the areas of a large shop that sells a kind of goods
senses.definitionCN: 大商店里售卖某一类商品的区域
senses.example: The store has a whole department for kitchen goods.
senses.exampleCN: 这家商店有一整块区域卖厨房用品。
senses.why: A shop that sells everything must sort itself like a small city.
senses.whyCN: 什么都卖的商店，得像座小城那样把自己归类。

intro.en: Department came from French département, which grew out of départir, to divide or share out.
intro.cn: department 来自法语 département，而它又由 départir（划分、分配）长出来。

items.en: Departement came from departir, to divide or share out.
items.cn: departement 来自 departir，意为划分或分配。

items.en: The word named an administrative division of the state.
items.cn: 这个词指国家的行政区划。

items.en: English took department for a branch of government or business.
items.cn: 英语借来 department，指政府或企业的分支。

items.en: Universities and shops borrowed it for their own divisions.
items.cn: 大学与商店也借它来称呼自己的分区。

items.en: Now any large body can be cut into departments.
items.cn: 如今任何大的机构都能被切成部门。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the depart stem, and the meaning group gives three words for a part of something larger.
note.cn: 形近组共用 depart 词干，近义组则给出三个表示「大东西的一部分」的词。

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a floor plan cut into rooms and end with a shop that sorts everything by kind.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从被切成一个个房间的平面图开始，落到按类别整理万物的商店。

normal.en: A department is a slice of a big building.
normal.cn: 部门就是一栋大楼切下来的一片。

normal.en: The sign on the door tells you which slice you are in.
normal.cn: 门上的牌子告诉你，你在哪一片里。

normal.en: A university divides by subject, a shop by goods.
normal.cn: 大学按学科分，商店按货物分。

normal.en: Department and departure share the same parting root.
normal.cn: department 与 departure 共用同一个「分开」的词根。

normal.en: Too many people in one room is how departments begin.
normal.cn: 一间屋子挤了太多人，部门就是这样开始的。

abstract.en: Picture a map of a building with each room lit a different colour.
abstract.cn: 想象一张楼内地图，每个房间亮着不同颜色。

abstract.en: Picture a long corridor with names painted above every door.
abstract.cn: 想象一条长走廊，每扇门上方都刷着名字。

abstract.en: Picture shelves sorted until nothing is out of place.
abstract.cn: 想象货架被整理到没有一样东西放错。

examples.en: She works in the sales department of a small company.
examples.cn: 她在小公司的销售部工作。

examples.en: She teaches in the history department.
examples.cn: 她在历史系任教。

examples.en: The store has a whole department for kitchen goods.
examples.cn: 这家商店有一整块区域卖厨房用品。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 department 记成「地面切成块」：de 是分开，part 是部分，一个大机构被分成一块块，就是部门。

root: 来自法语 département，源头是 départir（划分、分配）。它先指国家的行政区划，十八世纪进入英语后指政府或企业的分支，十九世纪又被大学与商店借去称呼各自的划分。

sensesIntro.en: From an office divided by function, to a university divided by subject, to a shop divided by goods.
sensesIntro.cn: 从按职能划分的办公室，到按学科划分的大学，再到按货物划分的商店。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a floor plan cut into rooms, each with its own lamp.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张被切成房间的平面图，每间亮着自己的灯。

branches.en: The first sense is work cut into manageable parts.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是把工作切成管得过来的几块。

branches.en: The second sense is knowledge cut by subject.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是把知识按学科切开。

branches.en: The third sense is goods cut by kind.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是把货物按种类分开。

branches.en: An office and a university both divide because one voice cannot hold everything.
branches.cn: 办公室与大学都要划分，因为一个声音装不下所有事。

branches.en: A subject and a shelf are both sorting devices.
branches.cn: 学科与货架，都是分类的工具。

intro.en: Department belongs to the parting family and carries the idea of division into organized life.
intro.cn: department 属于「分开」这一族，把划分的观念带进组织生活。

latinIntro.en: The base is partire, to divide, seen also in part and partial.
latinIntro.cn: 它的词基是 partire（划分），在 part 与 partial 里也能看到。

items.meaning: a large shop with many sections

definition_zh: adj. 部门的；部（司、局）的；按部门划分的
definition_en: relating to or organised by a department of an organisation

pos.zh: 部门的；部（司、局）的；按部门划分的

senses.title: Of a department

senses.title: Organised by departments

senses.why: A corridor with a different sign on each door.

senses.title: Within one department only

senses.why: A memo circulated inside one floor only.
senses.whyCN: 一份只在一层楼内传阅的备忘录。

intro.en: Departmental is department plus -al; department is depart plus -ment, from Latin partiri, to divide.
intro.cn: departmental 由 department 加 -al 构成；department 由 depart 加 -ment 构成，源自拉丁语 partiri（分开）。

items.en: Pars meant a part or share.
items.cn: pars 意为部分、份额。

items.en: Partiri meant to divide or share out.
items.cn: partiri 意为分开、分配。

items.en: Depart entered English for dividing and then leaving.
items.cn: 十五世纪 depart 先指分开，后指离开。

items.en: Department named a separate division of a whole.
items.cn: 十八世纪 department 指整体中分出的一个部分。

items.en: Departmental was formed as its adjective.
items.cn: 十九世纪 departmental 作为其形容词被造出。

items.en: It is standard in universities and government.
items.cn: 如今在大学与政府中是标准用语。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the part- dividing family; the near-meaning group names other ways of being limited to a section.

normal.en: Part- means a part, as in partition.

examples.en: The change was departmental, not university-wide.

sensesIntro.cn: 同一个被分开的整体：一枚章、一条走廊与一份备忘录。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a corridor of doors each with a different department sign, a file collecting three stamps

branches.en: A stamp passed across three desks.

branches.en: Both show a whole split into named parts.

branches.en: Both keep things inside one boundary.
branches.cn: 两者都把事情留在一条边界之内。

intro.en: Departmental is de- plus part- plus -ment plus -al; the part root builds the dividing family.
intro.cn: departmental 由 de- 加 part- 加 -ment 加 -al 构成；部分这个词根造出划分一族词。

latinIntro.en: Latin pars means a part, partiri to divide and secare to cut.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pars 意为部分，partiri 意为分开，secare 意为切。

definition_en: the act of leaving a place, or a change away from what is usual
core_image: 机场大屏上一行行航班变成灰色，登机口空了下来
scene: 广播念出航班号，候机的人陆续站起来，椅子一排排空下去。Her departure left the office very quiet.
sceneCN: 这里 departure 指「离开」（第 1 个义项：离开某地的行为）；句意是她的离开让办公室安静下来。

senses.title: The act of leaving
senses.definition: the act of going away from a place
senses.definitionCN: 从某地走开的行为
senses.example: Her departure left the office very quiet.
senses.exampleCN: 她的离开让办公室安静下来。
senses.why: A leaving is felt most by the people who stay.
senses.whyCN: 离开这件事，留在原地的人感受最深。

senses.title: The start of a journey
senses.definition: the moment when a journey or flight begins
senses.definitionCN: 旅程或航班开始的时刻
senses.example: The departure time is printed on the ticket.
senses.exampleCN: 票上印着出发时间。
senses.why: A journey has to be dated from somewhere.
senses.whyCN: 旅程总得从一个时刻算起。

senses.title: A turn away from the old
senses.definition: a change that leaves the usual way behind
senses.definitionCN: 离开通常做法的改变
senses.example: The new design is a departure from tradition.
senses.exampleCN: 新设计是对传统的一次背离。
senses.why: Not every departure needs a station; an idea can leave too.
senses.whyCN: 不是每次离开都需要车站，想法也会出走。

items.en: Departir meant to divide, to separate or to leave.

items.en: Departure named a separation or a going away.

items.en: English used departure for the act of leaving.
items.cn: 英语用 departure 表示离开这一行为。

items.en: Travel gave it a fixed place beside arrival.
items.cn: 旅行让它与到达并列，各占一头。

normal.en: An empty gate is a departure you can see.

abstract.en: Picture a row of chairs with coats lifted off them.
abstract.cn: 想象一排椅子，上面的外套被一件件拿走。

abstract.en: Picture a gate number still glowing after the flight has gone.
abstract.cn: 想象航班走了，登机口号码还亮着。

abstract.en: Picture a road forking away from a straight line.
abstract.cn: 想象一条路从直线上岔开。

examples.en: Her departure left the office very quiet.
examples.cn: 她的离开让办公室安静下来。

examples.en: The departure time is printed on the ticket.
examples.cn: 票上印着出发时间。

examples.en: The new design is a departure from tradition.
examples.cn: 新设计是对传统的一次背离。

sensesIntro.en: From a gate that empties, to a time printed on a ticket, to a design that leaves the old path.

core.cn: 核心意象：一排空椅子上方，登机口号码还亮着。

branches.en: The first sense is the plain fact of someone going.
branches.cn: 第一个义项就是有人走了这个朴素事实。

branches.en: The second sense is the clock time when a journey starts.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是旅程开始的钟点。

branches.en: The third sense is a method or habit left behind.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是被留在身后的方法或习惯。

branches.en: Every journey begins as a leaving, with a time attached.
branches.cn: 每段旅程都从一次离开开始，还带着一个时间。

branches.en: A person and a design can both depart from what was expected.
branches.cn: 人与设计，都可能从预期里走出去。

intro.en: Departure is the noun of leaving, standing beside depart and the whole parting family.
intro.cn: departure 是表示离开的名词，与 depart 以及整个「分开」家族站在一起。

latinIntro.en: The base is partire, to divide; -ure turns the act into a noun.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是 partire（划分），-ure 把这个动作变成名词。

items.meaning: having left, or no longer living
a part of a large organization
items.example: She works in the sales department.
The departmental meeting is at nine.

items.meaning: a waiting room before a flight
items.example: We met in the departure lounge.

items.meaning: the gate for a leaving flight

definition_en: to need someone or something for support, or to be decided by something
core_image: 一根细杆斜靠在墙上，整面重量都压在墙那一点
scene: 老桥的一侧靠在山壁上，另一侧悬着，木板随脚步轻响。Whether we go out depends on the weather.
sceneCN: 这里 depend 指「取决于」（第 2 个义项：由某事决定）；句意是我们是否出门取决于天气。

senses.title: Need support
senses.definition: to need someone or something in order to manage
senses.definitionCN: 为了应付需要某人或某物
senses.example: Young children depend on their parents for food.
senses.exampleCN: 幼儿依靠父母获得食物。
senses.why: A thing that leans cannot stand without the thing it leans on.
senses.whyCN: 靠着别人的东西，离了那面墙就站不住。

senses.title: Be decided by
senses.definition: to be decided or affected by something else
senses.definitionCN: 由另一件事决定或受影响
senses.example: Whether we go out depends on the weather.
senses.exampleCN: 我们是否出门取决于天气。
senses.why: The answer is not in the question; it waits in another fact.
senses.whyCN: 答案不在问题里，而在另一个事实那里等着。

senses.title: Trust someone
senses.definition: to trust someone to do what is needed
senses.definitionCN: 相信某人会做好该做的事
senses.example: You can depend on her to keep a secret.
senses.exampleCN: 你可以信赖她保守秘密。
senses.why: Trust is leaning on a person and finding them solid.
senses.whyCN: 信任就是靠上一个人，发现他站得住。

intro.en: Depend comes from Latin dependere, to hang down, built from de-, down, and pendere, to hang.
intro.cn: depend 来自拉丁语 dependere（悬垂），由 de-（向下）与 pendere（悬挂）组成。

items.en: Dependere meant to hang down or hang from something.
items.cn: dependere 意为垂下或从某物上悬挂。

items.en: Writers used it for things that rested on other things.
items.cn: 作家用它指依附在别的东西上的事物。

items.en: English took depend for leaning on support.
items.cn: 英语借来 depend，表示倚靠支撑。

items.en: It grew the sense of being decided by a condition.
items.cn: 它长出了「由某个条件决定」的意思。

items.en: Now it covers need, condition and trust.
items.cn: 如今它覆盖需要、条件与信任。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the pend- stem of hanging, and the meaning group gives three ways of leaning on something.
note.cn: 形近组共用表示悬挂的 pend- 词干，近义组则给出三种倚靠的说法。

entries.definition: needing support from someone else
the state of needing support
able to be trusted
to need and trust someone or something
entries.definitionCN: 需要并信任某人或某物

entries.definition: to expect something to happen
to be decided by one thing

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a pole leaning against a wall and end with a person you can lean on.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一根靠在墙上的杆子开始，落到一个你可以靠的人。

normal.en: De- is down and pend- is hang: to depend is to hang from something.
normal.cn: de- 是向下，pend- 是悬挂，depend 就是吊在某样东西上。

normal.en: A bridge that leans on a cliff does not argue with the cliff.
normal.cn: 靠在山壁上的桥，不会跟山壁争辩。

normal.en: The answer depends on a fact you have not checked yet.
normal.cn: 答案取决于一个你还没去核实的事实。

normal.en: A dependable person is a wall that does not move.
normal.cn: 可靠的人，就是一堵不会动的墙。

normal.en: Depend and dependent differ only in their ending.
normal.cn: depend 与 dependent 只差一个词尾。

abstract.en: Picture a ladder resting on one narrow ledge.
abstract.cn: 想象一把梯子只靠在一道窄窄的凸沿上。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp hanging from a single wire.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯只由一根线吊着。

abstract.en: Picture two people walking, one holding the other's arm.
abstract.cn: 想象两个人走路，一个扶着另一个的胳膊。

examples.en: Young children depend on their parents for food.
examples.cn: 幼儿依靠父母获得食物。

examples.en: Whether we go out depends on the weather.
examples.cn: 我们是否出门取决于天气。

examples.en: You can depend on her to keep a secret.
examples.cn: 你可以信赖她保守秘密。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 depend 记成「吊在下面」：pend 是悬挂，de 是向下，整个人吊在别人身上，就是依靠。

root: 来自拉丁语 dependere，由 de-（向下）与 pendere（悬挂）组成。本义是垂下、从某物上悬挂，后来引申为倚靠支撑；十七世纪又长出「由某个条件决定」的意思，现代还用来表示对人的信赖。

sensesIntro.en: From a pole leaning on a wall, to an answer waiting on a fact, to a person you can trust.
sensesIntro.cn: 从靠在墙上的杆子，到等一个事实的答案，再到一个可以信任的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin pole leans and gives all its weight to one wall.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根细杆斜靠着，把全部重量交给一面墙。

branches.en: The first sense is weight resting on another thing.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是重量落在另一样东西上。

branches.en: The second sense is a result waiting on a condition.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是结果在等一个条件。

branches.en: The third sense is a person who will hold when you lean.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是你靠上去时撑得住的人。

branches.en: A bridge and an answer both rest on something outside themselves.
branches.cn: 桥与答案，都落在自身之外的某样东西上。

branches.en: To depend on a fact and on a friend are two kinds of trust.
branches.cn: 依赖一个事实与依赖一个朋友，是两种信任。

intro.en: Depend has a large family of hanging and leaning words, from dependence to independence.
intro.cn: depend 有一大族表示悬挂与倚靠的词，从依赖一直到独立。

latinIntro.en: The base is pendere, to hang, with de- meaning down; the same root gives pendant and suspend.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是 pendere（悬挂），de- 表示向下；同一词根还给出 pendant 与 suspend。

items.meaning: to need or be decided by
items.example: We depend on the river for water.

items.exampleCN: 这个孩子仍然依赖他人。

items.meaning: a state of relying on another
items.example: The island was once a dependency.
The two towns live in interdependence.

definition_en: the state of needing or being supported by someone or something else, or of being decided by another factor
core_image: 一根细绳把吊灯吊在天花板的钩子上，灯的全部重量都落在那个钩子上
scene: 补给船延误了，岛上的空油罐排在码头边：The island's dependence on imported fuel became clear when the supply ship was delayed.
sceneCN: 这里 dependence 是「依赖」（第 1 个义项：需要外部供给才能维持）；句意：补给船延误时，这座岛对外来燃料的依赖就暴露无遗。图中可辨识物件：小岛码头、空油罐、延误的补给船、等待卸货的吊车。

pos.zh: 依赖；依靠；依赖性；从属关系

forms.label: 不可数用法（表示状态时通常不可数）

senses.title: The state of relying on something
senses.titleCN: 依赖：重量挂在别人身上
senses.definition: the condition of needing another person or thing in order to function or survive
senses.definitionCN: 为了运作或生存而需要另一人或物的状态
senses.example: The village's dependence on the single well shaped its daily life.
senses.exampleCN: 全村对这口唯一水井的依赖塑造了它的日常生活。
senses.why: dependere means 'to hang down from'. A lamp hangs from a hook, and its weight rests on that hook; dependence is that hanging relationship turned into a state noun.
senses.whyCN: dependere 意为“悬挂于……之下”。吊灯挂在钩子上，全部重量压在钩子上；dependence 就是把这种悬挂关系变成状态名词。

senses.title: Economic reliance
senses.definition: a situation in which an economy needs another economy for trade, finance or supply
senses.definitionCN: 一个经济体在贸易、金融或供给上需要另一经济体的状况
senses.example: The country's dependence on a single export made it fragile.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家依赖单一出口商品，因此十分脆弱。
senses.why: An economy that leans on one buyer is like a lamp with one hook. The de- prefix points downward, the direction in which support must come.
senses.whyCN: 只靠一个买家的经济体就像只有一只钩子的吊灯。de- 前缀指向下方，也就是支撑必须来自的方向。

senses.title: Drug or alcohol dependence
senses.titleCN: 药物依赖：身体已经离不开
senses.definition: a medical condition in which a person needs a substance and cannot stop without distress
senses.definitionCN: 一种医学状态，患者需要某种物质，停用即出现痛苦
senses.example: Long-term use can lead to physical dependence on the painkiller.
senses.exampleCN: 长期使用可能导致对止痛药的身体依赖。
senses.why: The medical sense keeps the hanging image: the body has attached its normal function to a chemical hook. Removal of the hook produces withdrawal.
senses.whyCN: 医学义保留了悬挂意象：身体把正常功能挂在某个化学钩子上。钩子一撤，就出现戒断反应。

senses.title: Mutual reliance
senses.titleCN: 相互依赖：两根柱子互相撑着
senses.definition: a relationship in which two parties each need the other
senses.definitionCN: 双方各自都需要对方的关系
senses.example: The two industries developed a mutual dependence that neither could easily break.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个行业发展出一种彼此都难以轻易切断的相互依赖。
senses.why: Two hanging objects can support each other, so the single hook becomes a pair of hooks. The noun still names a support relation, now symmetrical.
senses.whyCN: 两个悬挂物可以互相支撑，于是单钩变成一对钩子。这个名词仍命名支撑关系，只是现在是对称的。

senses.title: Statistical dependence
senses.titleCN: 统计依赖性：一个变量的变化牵着另一个
senses.definition: in statistics, the condition in which one variable's value is related to another's
senses.definitionCN: 统计学中一个变量的取值与另一个变量相关的状态
senses.example: The study tested the dependence of rainfall on ocean temperature.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究检验了降雨对海洋温度的依赖性。
senses.why: A dependent variable hangs from an independent one: change the anchor and the hanging value moves. The statistical term borrows the same geometry.
senses.whyCN: 因变量悬挂在自变量上：锚点一动，悬挂的值就动。统计术语借用了同一套几何关系。

senses.title: Emotional reliance
senses.titleCN: 情感依赖：心里那根绳子
senses.definition: a psychological need for another person's approval, presence or support
senses.definitionCN: 在心理上需要他人的认可、陪伴或支持
senses.example: His emotional dependence made it hard for him to make decisions alone.
senses.exampleCN: 他的情感依赖让他很难独自做决定。
senses.why: The support here is not physical weight but reassurance. The metaphor still works because the person's confidence is felt to hang from someone else.
senses.whyCN: 这里的支撑不是物理重量，而是安心感。隐喻仍然成立，因为这个人的信心被感觉成挂在别人身上。

senses.title: Technological reliance
senses.titleCN: 技术依赖：关键零件握在别人手里
senses.definition: the condition of needing foreign technology, components or expertise
senses.definitionCN: 需要外国技术、零部件或专业能力的状况
senses.example: Dependence on imported chips slowed the factory's expansion.
senses.exampleCN: 对进口芯片的依赖拖慢了工厂的扩张。
senses.why: Supply chains are chains of hooks: each stage holds the next. When a link is foreign, the whole structure leans outward.
senses.whyCN: 供应链是一串钩子：每一环吊着下一环。当某一环在海外，整个结构就向外倾斜。

senses.title: Subordinate status
senses.titleCN: 从属地位：名义上自主，实际受管
senses.definition: the status of a territory or institution that is controlled by another
senses.definitionCN: 领地或机构受另一者控制的地位
senses.example: The report described the region's long dependence on the colonial administration.
senses.exampleCN: 报告描述了该地区对殖民当局的长期从属。
senses.why: Political dependence is the institutional version of hanging: the smaller unit has no independent footing and takes its orders from above.
senses.whyCN: 政治上的从属是悬挂的制度版：较小单位没有独立立足点，命令来自上方。

intro.en: Dependence goes back to Latin dependere, built from de- 'down' and pendere 'to hang'. The literal 'hang down from' became 'rely on' in Late Latin and French, and English borrowed the state noun in the 16th century.
intro.cn: dependence 可追到拉丁 dependere，由 de-“向下”和 pendere“悬挂”构成。字面的“挂在……下面”在晚期拉丁语和法语中变成“依靠”，英语在 16 世纪借入了这个状态名词。

items.en: pendere meant 'to hang, be suspended'. It also gave pendulum and pendant, both visibly hanging objects, so the physical image is present across the family.
items.cn: pendere 意为“悬挂、被吊起”。它还派生了 pendulum 和 pendant，两者都是明显悬挂的物体，因此整个词族都带着这个物理画面。

items.en: dependere adds de- 'down from', giving 'to hang down from, be attached to'. Classical Latin used it of things physically suspended from a point.
items.cn: dependere 加 de-“从……向下”，意为“挂在……下面、附着于”。古典拉丁语用它描述实际悬挂在某个点上的东西。

items.en: The step from 'hang from' to 'rely on' is metaphorical: whatever hangs from a support cannot stand without it. Late Latin and French extend the verb to persons and conditions.
items.cn: 从“悬挂于”到“依靠”的转变是隐喻性的：挂在支撑物上的东西离开支撑就站不住。晚期拉丁语和法语把这个动词扩展到人和处境。

items.en: Dependence enters English in the 16th century as the state noun of depend. The exact first date is uncertain because dependence and dependency competed in spelling and meaning.
items.cn: dependence 在 16 世纪作为 depend 的状态名词进入英语。由于 dependence 与 dependency 在拼写和意义上长期竞争，确切的最早年代存疑。

items.en: In the 20th century, medicine standardized drug dependence for the physiological need for a substance, separating it from addiction as a broader behavioural term.
items.cn: 20 世纪，医学界用 drug dependence 固定指对某物质的生理需要，以便与范围更广的行为术语 addiction 区分。

items.en: Statistical dependence was named in the same period: variables that are not independent are said to depend on one another, keeping the anchor image.
items.cn: 统计学的“依赖性”也在同一时期得名：不独立的变量被说成彼此依赖，保留了锚点意象。

note.en: The look-alike group contains the same pend- family with different endings; the near-meaning group shares the idea of needing support but names different kinds of need.
note.cn: 形近组是同一 pend- 词族的不同词尾；近义组都含“需要支撑”的意思，但指的需要类型不同。

entries.definition: a state of reliance, a dependent territory, or a required software component. It overlaps with dependence but is more countable and more technical.
entries.definitionCN: 依赖状态、属地，或软件依赖项。它与 dependence 重叠，但更可数、更技术化。

entries.definition: relying on another; also a person who is supported by someone else. It describes the one who hangs, not the relation itself.
entries.definitionCN: 依赖的；亦指受抚养人。它描述“悬挂者”，而不是关系本身。

entries.definition: reliable and trustworthy. The -able suffix shifts the meaning from 'needing support' to 'able to be relied on'.
entries.definitionCN: 可靠的；可信赖的。-able 后缀把意义从“需要支撑”转成“可以被依靠”。

entries.definition: the state of depending on someone or something, often with trust; it stresses confidence more than structural necessity.
entries.definitionCN: 对某人或某物的依赖，常带信任意味；它比结构性必需更强调信心。

entries.definition: a strong compulsive need for a substance or activity; broader and more behavioural than drug dependence.
entries.definitionCN: 对某物质或活动的强烈强迫性需要；比 drug dependence 范围更广，更偏行为层面。

entries.definition: mutual dependence between parties; it names the two-way version of the same hanging relation.
entries.definitionCN: 各方之间的相互依赖；它命名的是同一悬挂关系的双向版本。

entries.definition: the state of being lower in rank or under another's authority; it concerns power, while dependence concerns need.
entries.definitionCN: 地位较低或受他人管辖的状态；它关乎权力，而 dependence 关乎需要。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配和真实同族词，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: de- 'down' + pendere 'hang': dependence is the state of hanging from a support.
normal.cn: de-“向下”+ pendere“悬挂”：dependence 就是挂在支撑物下面的状态。

normal.en: pendulum and pendant are visible cousins: they hang, and dependence names what hanging means for people.
normal.cn: pendulum 和 pendant 是看得见的同族词：它们都悬挂，而 dependence 命名“悬挂”对人意味着什么。

normal.en: The usual preposition is on, which matches the image: the lamp hangs on the hook.
normal.cn: 常用介词是 on，正好对应画面：灯挂在钩子上（hangs on the hook）。

normal.en: dependent is the adjective, dependence the state noun, dependency the countable or territorial noun; keep the endings apart.
normal.cn: dependent 是形容词，dependence 是状态名词，dependency 是可数或属地名词；词尾要分清。

normal.en: independence is the same image with the negative prefix: no hook, standing on its own.
normal.cn: independence 是同一画面加否定前缀：没有钩子，自己站住。

abstract.en: Think of a single nail holding a heavy picture frame: remove the nail and the frame falls.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚钉子挂着沉重的画框：钉子一拔，画框就掉。

abstract.en: Think of a climber clipped to one rope: every move is safe only while the rope holds.
abstract.cn: 想象攀岩者只扣在一根绳上：只要绳子还牢，每个动作才安全。

abstract.en: Think of two drunks holding each other up: neither can walk alone, which is mutual dependence.
abstract.cn: 想象两个醉汉互相扶着走：谁也不能独自走，这就是相互依赖。

examples.en: Reducing dependence on imported oil became the government's main energy goal.
examples.cn: 减少对进口石油的依赖成了政府的主要能源目标。

examples.en: The doctor warned that dependence on sleeping pills can develop quickly.
examples.cn: 医生警告说，对安眠药的依赖可能很快形成。

examples.en: Their friendship rested on a healthy dependence rather than on control.
examples.cn: 他们的友谊建立在健康的依赖之上，而不是控制之上。

dict_mnemonic.text: “地喷den斯”——地上（de）喷出的喷泉（pen）全靠水泵撑着 → dependence 依赖、依靠

root: 拉丁 dependere“挂在……下面、依附”（de-“向下”+ pendere“悬挂”）；depend- 词干 + -ence 状态名词后缀。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one geometry: something hangs from a support, and its ability to stay in place belongs to that support.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享同一套几何关系：某物挂在支撑上，它能否留在原位取决于那个支撑。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a weight hanging from a single hook.
core.cn: 核心意象：重量挂在唯一一只钩子上。

branches.en: TWO HOOKS: mutual reliance is the same hanging relation drawn with two supports.
branches.cn: 两只钩子：相互依赖是同一悬挂关系画成双支撑。

branches.en: ECONOMIC AND TECHNICAL SUPPORT: an economy leaning on one export and a factory leaning on imported chips both hang outward.
branches.cn: 经济与技术支撑：依赖单一出口的经济体和依赖进口芯片的工厂，都向外悬挂。

branches.en: BODY AND MIND: chemical dependence and emotional dependence attach normal functioning to a hook outside the self.
branches.cn: 身体与心理：药物依赖与情感依赖都把正常运转挂到自我之外的钩子上。

branches.en: STATISTICS AND POLITICS: a dependent variable and a dependent territory both take their position from a stronger anchor.
branches.cn: 统计与政治：因变量与属地都从更强的锚点那里取得自己的位置。

branches.en: THE BASE SENSE: every extension keeps the original 'hanging' meaning and adds only the kind of support involved.
branches.cn: 基础义：每个引申都保留最初的“悬挂”含义，只增加所涉及的支撑类型。

intro.en: Dependence is depend plus -ence, a Latin-derived state suffix. Both de- and pendere are fossilized inside the base; English adds only -ence, and -ent or -ency for related forms.
intro.cn: dependence 是 depend 加 -ence（源自拉丁的状态后缀）。de- 与 pendere 都已凝固在词基内；英语只加 -ence，相关形式则用 -ent 或 -ency。

latinIntro.en: Latin pendere 'to hang' yields pendulus 'hanging', dependere 'hang from', and the noun dependens. The stem pend- also appears in pendulum, pendant and suspend.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 pendere“悬挂”派生 pendulus“悬挂的”、dependere“挂在……下”以及名词 dependens。词干 pend- 也出现在 pendulum、pendant、suspend 中。

items.meaning: to hang from; to rely on
items.meaningCN: 悬挂于；依赖；取决于（de-“向下”+ pendere“悬挂”）
items.example: The harvest depends on how much rain falls in spring.
items.exampleCN: 收成取决于春季降雨量。

items.meaning: relying on another; supported by another
items.meaningCN: 依赖的；受抚养的（-ent 构成形容词）
items.example: A dependent child must be listed on the form.
items.exampleCN: 受抚养子女必须填在表格上。

items.meaning: the state of relying on something
items.meaningCN: 依赖；依靠（-ence 构成状态名词）
items.example: Dependence on a single supplier is a business risk.
items.exampleCN: 依赖单一供应商是一种商业风险。

items.meaning: reliance; a dependent territory; a required component
items.meaningCN: 依赖；属地；依赖项（-ency 构成状态或事物名词）
items.example: The software update broke an old dependency.
items.exampleCN: 这次软件更新破坏了一个旧的依赖项。

items.example: The old generator is noisy but dependable.
items.exampleCN: 那台旧发电机很吵，但很可靠。

items.meaningCN: 可靠地（-ly 构成方式副词）
items.example: The bus arrives dependably at seven each morning.
items.exampleCN: 这趟公交每天早上七点准点到。

items.meaningCN: 独立的；不受支配的（in-“不”+ dependent）
items.example: The laboratory is independent of the manufacturer.
items.exampleCN: 该实验室独立于制造商。

items.example: Global trade rests on a web of interdependence.
items.exampleCN: 全球贸易建立在一张相互依赖的网上。

items.cn: pendere 意为悬挂。

items.en: Dependere meant to hang down from.

scene: 孩子还小，出门要牵着大人的手，过马路也要人抱。The plant is dependent on light from the window.
sceneCN: 这里 dependent 指「依赖的」（第 1 个义项：需要他人或他物支持）；句意是这株植物依赖窗外的光。

senses.title: Needing support
senses.definition: needing someone or something in order to live or work
senses.definitionCN: 为了生活或运转需要他人或他物的
senses.example: The plant is dependent on light from the window.
senses.exampleCN: 这株植物依赖窗外的光。
senses.why: A plant in a window turns toward what it cannot make for itself.
senses.whyCN: 窗边的植物会转向它自己造不出来的东西。

senses.title: Decided by something
senses.definition: decided or affected by something else
senses.definitionCN: 由另一件事决定或受其影响的
senses.example: The price is dependent on the season.
senses.exampleCN: 价格取决于季节。
senses.why: A dependent price has no will of its own.
senses.whyCN: 取决于别处的价格，没有自己的主意。

senses.title: A person who is supported
senses.definition: a person, often a child, who is supported by another
senses.definitionCN: 由他人供养的人，常指孩子
senses.example: The policy helps workers with dependents.
senses.exampleCN: 这项政策帮助有受抚养人的工作者。
senses.why: The noun names the one who leans, not the leaning.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词命名的是靠着的人，而不是靠着这件事。

intro.en: Dependent is the adjective formed from Latin dependere, to hang from, with the ending -ent.
intro.cn: dependent 由拉丁语 dependere（悬挂于）加形容词词尾 -ent 构成。

items.en: Dependere meant to hang down from a support.
items.cn: dependere 意为从支撑物上垂下。

items.en: The adjective dependens described what hung from something.
items.cn: 形容词 dependens 形容从某物上悬着的东西。

items.en: English used dependent for leaning on support.
items.cn: 英语用 dependent 表示倚靠支撑。

items.en: Grammar borrowed the word for a clause that needs another.
items.cn: 语法学借它指需要另一句才能成立的从句。

items.en: Now it also names a person who is supported.
items.cn: 如今它也指一个由他人供养的人。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the depend stem, and the meaning group gives words for relying and for being conditional.
note.cn: 形近组共用 depend 词干，近义组则给出表示依靠与有条件的词。

normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从缠在竹竿上的藤蔓开始，落到一个跟着季节走的价格。

normal.en: A vine with no pole has nowhere to climb.
normal.cn: 没有竹竿的藤蔓，没地方往上爬。

normal.en: Dependent looks like depend plus an ending, because it is.
normal.cn: dependent 看起来就是 depend 加个词尾，因为它本来如此。

normal.en: A dependent price is a leaf in the wind.
normal.cn: 取决于别处的价格，是风里的一片叶子。

normal.en: The noun dependent means the person, not the need.
normal.cn: 名词 dependent 指的是那个人，不是那份需要。

normal.en: Add in- and the leaning stops: independent.
normal.cn: 前面加 in-，倚靠就停了：independent。

abstract.cn: 想象一株小苗被绑在一根直棍上。

abstract.en: Picture a hand holding the back of a bicycle seat.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手扶着自行车后座。

abstract.en: Picture a price tag turning with the calendar.
abstract.cn: 想象价签跟着日历翻动。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 dependent 记成「吊着的人」：depend 是悬挂依靠，ent 是人或物，吊在别人身上的，就是依赖的。

root: 来自拉丁语 dependere（悬挂于）加形容词词尾 -ent。它先形容从支撑物上垂下的东西，十五世纪进入英语表示倚靠，十八世纪语法学借它指需要另一句的从句，现代又用作名词指受抚养的人。

sensesIntro.en: From a vine on a pole, to a price on a season, to a child in someone's care.
sensesIntro.cn: 从缠在竿上的藤，到跟着季节的价格，再到被人照顾的孩子。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a vine hangs all its weight on one bamboo pole.
core.cn: 核心意象：一株藤把全部重量挂在一根竹竿上。

branches.en: The first sense is living support, the way a vine needs a pole.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是活生生的支撑，像藤需要竿。

branches.en: The second sense is a result that moves with another fact.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是跟着另一个事实移动的结果。

branches.en: The third sense turns the adjective into a person.
branches.cn: 第三个义项把这个形容词变成了一个人。

branches.en: Plants and prices both answer to something outside themselves.
branches.cn: 植物与价格，都听命于自身之外的某样东西。

branches.en: A dependent person and a dependent price both lack a free hand.
branches.cn: 受抚养的人与取决于别处的价格，都没有自由的手。

intro.en: Dependent sits inside the hanging family, next to depend and opposite independent.
intro.cn: dependent 位于「悬挂」家族之中，一边是 depend，另一边是 independent。

latinIntro.en: The base is pendere, to hang, with de- meaning down and -ent making an adjective.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是 pendere（悬挂），de- 表示向下，-ent 构成形容词。

definition_en: to show or represent something in a picture, a story or words
core_image: 一支笔在纸上落下第一道线，一个侧脸渐渐有了轮廓
scene: 墙上那幅画里，渔民正把网从水里拉起，绳索绷得很紧。The painting depicts fishermen hauling in their nets.
sceneCN: 这里 depict 指用图像表现一个场景（第 1 个义项：用图像描绘）；句意为这幅画描绘渔民收网的场景。

senses.title: Show in a picture
senses.definition: to represent a scene or person in a painting, drawing or photograph
senses.definitionCN: 在绘画、素描或照片中表现场景或人物
senses.example: The painting depicts fishermen hauling in their nets.
senses.exampleCN: 这幅画描绘渔民收网的场景。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant 'to paint'; the hand and the pigment are the oldest part of the word.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为「绘画」；手与颜料是这个词最古老的部分。

senses.title: Describe in words
senses.definition: to describe something in speech or writing
senses.definitionCN: 用言语或文字描述某事物
senses.example: The novel depicts village life in the last century.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说描述了上个世纪的乡村生活。
senses.why: Words paint too: the same verb serves the brush and the pen because both make a scene visible.
senses.whyCN: 文字也在作画：同一个动词服务画笔与钢笔，因为两者都让场景变得可见。

senses.title: Portray a character
senses.definition: to present a person in a story with particular traits
senses.definitionCN: 在故事中呈现具有特定特征的人物
senses.example: The author depicts her as generous but proud.
senses.exampleCN: 作者把她刻画得慷慨却骄傲。
senses.why: A character is built line by line, and the word covers the accumulation of those lines.
senses.whyCN: 人物是一笔一笔建起来的，这个词涵盖的就是这些笔画的累积。

senses.title: Represent symbolically
senses.definition: to stand for something larger through an image
senses.definitionCN: 通过图像代表更宏大的事物
senses.example: The mural depicts peace as a white bird over ruins.
senses.exampleCN: 壁画把和平表现为废墟上的一只白鸟。
senses.why: A symbol is a picture that carries more than it shows, and depiction is how that load is attached.
senses.whyCN: 象征是一幅承载多于其所显示之物的画，而描绘就是附上这份重量的方式。

senses.title: Present a scene vividly
senses.definition: to set a scene before the reader's or viewer's mind
senses.definitionCN: 把场景呈现在读者或观者心中
senses.example: The opening chapter depicts a storm at sea.
senses.exampleCN: 开篇一章呈现了海上风暴。
senses.why: Vividness depends on selection: a few details make the whole scene appear.
senses.whyCN: 生动取决于取舍：少数细节就能让整个场景浮现。

senses.title: Reflect accurately
senses.definition: to show something as it really is, without distortion
senses.definitionCN: 不失真地显示事物的真实样貌
senses.example: The report depicts conditions in the camp honestly.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告如实反映了营地里的状况。
senses.why: When accuracy is the goal, depiction becomes a test of honesty rather than skill.
senses.whyCN: 当目标是准确时，描绘就成了对诚实的检验，而不只是对技巧的检验。

senses.title: Portray in a certain light
senses.definition: to present someone or something with a chosen bias
senses.definitionCN: 带着选定的偏向呈现某人或某物
senses.example: The article depicts the reform as a disaster.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章把改革描绘成一场灾难。
senses.why: Every depiction chooses an angle, and the choice can be innocent or deliberate.
senses.whyCN: 每一种描绘都选了一个角度，而这个选择可以无辜，也可以是有意。

senses.title: Graphic representation
senses.definition: to represent data or structure by a diagram
senses.definitionCN: 用图表表现数据或结构
senses.example: The chart depicts the fall in prices over a year.
senses.exampleCN: 这张图展示了价格一年内的下跌。
senses.why: A diagram is depiction stripped to relations: no faces, only lines that show what connects to what.
senses.whyCN: 图表是被剥到只剩关系的描绘：没有面孔，只有显示连接关系的线。

intro.en: Depict comes from a Latin verb meaning to paint, and painting remains its core image.
intro.cn: depict 来自一个意为「绘画」的拉丁动词，绘画始终是它的核心意象。

items.en: English borrowed depict in the 17c. for painting and later extended it to writing and diagrams.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入 depict，指绘画，后来扩展到文字与图表。

items.en: Depingere meant 'to paint, portray', built from de- and pingere 'to paint'.
items.cn: depingere 意为「绘画、描绘」，由 de- 与 pingere「画」构成。

items.en: Pingere 'to paint' also gives picture and pigment, both about colour laid on a surface.
items.cn: pingere「画」也产生 picture 与 pigment，两者都关于涂在表面上的颜色。

items.en: Pictura meant 'painting' and supplied English pictura and pictorial through other routes.
items.cn: pictura 意为「绘画」，并通过其他路径提供英语的 pictorial 等词。

items.en: The verb widened from canvas to language, so that a sentence can depict a scene no one has painted.
items.cn: 这个动词从画布扩展到语言，于是一句话也可以描绘无人画过的场景。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the pict stem; the near-meaning group names ways of showing.
note.cn: 形近组共享 pict 词干；近义组列出各种呈现方式。

normal.cn: 想象画家用三笔勾出一张脸的轮廓。

normal.en: A diagram is a depiction with no faces, only connections.
normal.cn: 图表是没有面孔的描绘，只有连接。

normal.en: Say dih-PIKT, like a brush tapping the canvas.
normal.cn: 读成 dih-PIKT，像画笔点在画布上。

normal.en: Link it with describe: one paints for the eye, the other for the ear.
normal.cn: 把它和 describe 联系：一个为眼睛作画，一个为耳朵叙述。

abstract.en: Every depiction chooses an angle and leaves something out.
abstract.cn: 每一种描绘都选了一个角度，并遗漏了某些东西。

abstract.en: Words can paint a scene no one has ever seen.
abstract.cn: 文字可以画出无人见过的场景。

abstract.en: Accuracy in depiction is a form of honesty.
abstract.cn: 描绘中的准确，是一种诚实。

examples.en: The painting depicts fishermen hauling in their nets.
examples.cn: 这幅画描绘渔民收网的场景。

examples.en: The novel depicts village life in the last century.
examples.cn: 这部小说描述了上个世纪的乡村生活。

examples.en: The chart depicts the fall in prices over a year.
examples.cn: 这张图展示了价格一年内的下跌。

dict_mnemonic.text: de（向下）+ pict（画）：把形象画下来，就是「描绘」。

root: 拉丁语 depingere（绘画）：de- + pingere（画）

sensesIntro.en: Depict always makes something visible, whether to the eye or to the mind; the senses differ in the medium and in the honesty of the showing.
sensesIntro.cn: depict 始终让某物变得可见，无论对眼睛还是对心智；各义项的差别在于媒介，以及这种显示是否诚实。

core.en: MAKING A SCENE VISIBLE
core.cn: 让场景变得可见

branches.en: Pictures and vivid scenes made for the eye.
branches.cn: 为眼睛而作的图画与生动场景。

branches.en: Words that build a scene or a person.
branches.cn: 构建场景或人物的文字。

branches.en: Images that carry a meaning larger than themselves.
branches.cn: 承载着大于自身的意义的图像。

branches.en: Honest or slanted versions of the same thing.
branches.cn: 同一事物诚实或有偏向的版本。

branches.en: Diagrams that show only relations.
branches.cn: 只显示关系的图表。

intro.en: The word's family is built on the Latin verb for painting.
intro.cn: 这个词的词族建立在拉丁语「绘画」动词之上。

latinIntro.en: Latin pingere and pictura supply several English words about images and colour.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pingere 与 pictura 提供了若干关于图像与颜色的英语词。

items.meaning: the act or result of showing
items.example: The film's depiction of war is restrained.
items.exampleCN: 这部电影对战争的表现很克制。

items.meaning: shown in an image or account
items.meaningCN: 在图像或叙述中显示的
items.example: The scene is depicted in three panels.
items.exampleCN: 这个场景被画在三块板上。

items.example: A fresco depicting the harvest covers the wall.
items.exampleCN: 一幅描绘收获的壁画覆盖整面墙。
摄影是一种再现性的媒介。

items.example: The depicter of court life was a minor painter.
items.exampleCN: 这位描绘宫廷生活的人是个小画家。

items.example: The magazine is famous for its pictorial coverage.
items.exampleCN: 这本杂志以图片报道闻名。

items.example: The village is almost too picturesque.
items.exampleCN: 这个村庄几乎美得像画。
有些悲伤几乎无法表现。

definition_zh: v. 耗尽；使枯竭；大量减少（资源、存量）
definition_en: to reduce something greatly in number or quantity, especially a supply
core_image: 水库岸边露出一圈圈旧水位线，油罐的指针一点点往零走
scene: 干旱耗尽了水库的水。The drought depleted the reservoir.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：depleted 指耗尽；句意是干旱耗尽了水库的水。

senses.title: Use up a supply
senses.definition: to use up a supply until little is left
senses.definitionCN: 把供给用到所剩无几
senses.example: The drought depleted the reservoir.
senses.exampleCN: 干旱耗尽了水库的水。
senses.why: Old water lines showing on a dry bank.
senses.whyCN: 干涸岸边露出的一圈圈旧水位线。

senses.title: Reduce numbers
senses.definition: to reduce the number of people or things greatly
senses.definitionCN: 大幅减少人或物的数量
senses.example: Overfishing has depleted the cod stocks.
senses.exampleCN: 过度捕捞使鳕鱼资源枯竭。
senses.why: A net coming up nearly empty.
senses.whyCN: 一张几乎空着被拉上来的网。

senses.title: Weaken a body or fund
senses.definition: to drain strength, energy or money from something
senses.definitionCN: 把力气、精力或金钱从某处抽走
senses.example: The illness depleted her strength.
senses.exampleCN: 这场病耗尽了她的体力。
senses.why: A gauge needle creeping towards zero.
senses.whyCN: 一根一点点爬向零的指针。

intro.en: Deplete comes from Latin deplere, de- plus plere, to fill, from plenus, full: to empty what was full.
intro.cn: deplete 源自拉丁语 deplere，由 de- 加 plere（装满）构成，plere 来自 plenus（满的）：把满的倒空。

items.en: Plenus meant full.
items.cn: plenus 意为满的。

items.en: Plere meant to fill.
items.cn: plere 意为装满。

items.en: Deplere meant to empty out.
items.cn: deplere 意为倒空。

items.en: Deplete entered English for emptying a supply.
items.cn: 十七世纪 deplete 以耗空供给义进入英语。

items.en: It was used for draining resources and funds.
items.cn: 十九世纪用于资源与资金的耗减。

items.en: Ozone and fish stocks made it a common term.
items.cn: 臭氧与鱼类资源让它成为常用词。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the ple- filling family; the near-meaning group names other ways of emptying something.
note.cn: 形近组共享 ple-（装满）家族；近义组是其他「弄空」的说法。

entries.definition: The act of using up a supply.
To finish, or having all parts.
Filled or well supplied with something.
To use up completely.
To draw liquid or strength away.
To make or become smaller.

normalIntro.en: Deplete is de- away plus ple- full: take the fullness away until the gauge reads zero.
normalIntro.cn: deplete 就是 de-（去掉）加 ple-（满）：把满拿走，直到指针读零。

normal.en: Ple- means to fill, as in complete.
normal.cn: ple- 意为装满，如 complete。

normal.en: De- means away.
normal.cn: de- 表示去掉。

normal.en: Deplete a reservoir and the banks show.
normal.cn: 耗干水库，旧岸线就露出来。

normal.en: Overfishing depletes the stock.
normal.cn: 过度捕捞使鱼群枯竭。

normal.en: Illness depletes strength.
normal.cn: 疾病耗尽体力。

abstract.en: Old water lines showing on a dry bank.
abstract.cn: 干涸岸边露出的一圈圈旧水位线。

abstract.en: A net coming up nearly empty.
abstract.cn: 一张几乎空着被拉上来的网。

abstract.en: A gauge needle creeping towards zero.
abstract.cn: 一根一点点爬向零的指针。

examples.en: The war depleted the national reserves.
examples.cn: 战争耗尽了国家储备。

examples.en: Pumping is depleting the aquifer.
examples.cn: 抽水正在耗减地下水层。

examples.en: One bad season depletes the whole fund.
examples.cn: 一个坏年景就能耗空整笔基金。

dict_mnemonic.text: deplete 谐音「弟普立特」——不如记 de（去掉）＋ plete（满，与 complete 同根 plenus）＝把满的去掉，「耗尽、枯竭」。

root: 拉丁语 plenus（满）→ plere（装满）→ de-＋plere → deplere（倒空）→ 英语 deplete

sensesIntro.en: One fullness taken away: a reservoir, a fish stock and a body.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一份被拿走的满：一座水库、一群鱼与一个身体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: old water lines on a dry bank and a gauge needle creeping towards zero
core.cn: 核心意象：干涸岸边一圈圈旧水位线，指针一点点爬向零

branches.en: Old water lines showing on a dry bank.
branches.cn: 干涸岸边露出的一圈圈旧水位线。

branches.en: A net coming up nearly empty.
branches.cn: 一张几乎空着被拉上来的网。

branches.en: A gauge needle creeping towards zero.
branches.cn: 一根一点点爬向零的指针。

branches.en: Both take a stock down to very little.
branches.cn: 两者都把存量降到所剩无几。

branches.en: Both leave less than what was there before.
branches.cn: 两者都让剩下的比原先少。

intro.en: Deplete is de- plus ple-; the filling root builds the full and empty families.
intro.cn: deplete 由 de- 加 ple- 构成；装满这个词根造出满与空两族词。

latinIntro.en: Latin plenus means full, plere to fill and haurire to draw out.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 plenus 意为满，plere 意为装满，haurire 意为抽出。

definition_en: the reduction of a supply or quantity until little remains
core_image: 水库壁上留下一圈圈逐渐下降的旧水位线
scene: 干涸的水库岸边露出一圈圈旧水位线，原本淹在水下的坡面完全暴露。 The drought accelerated the depletion of the reservoir.
sceneCN: 这里 depletion 指「存量被持续取走而不断减少的过程」（第 1 个义项：供给或数量下降到所剩无几）；句意为干旱加速了水库水量的耗减。图中可辨识物件：层状水位线、裸露坡面、干裂泥面、远处坝体。

pos.zh: 耗竭；枯竭（可数或不可数）

derivatives.zh: 完整的；完成（同出 plere 词根）

senses.title: A supply being emptied
senses.definition: the process by which a supply or quantity is steadily reduced
senses.definitionCN: 供给或数量被持续减少的过程
senses.example: The drought accelerated the depletion of the reservoir.
senses.exampleCN: 干旱加速了水库水量的耗减。
senses.why: depletion comes from de- 'completely' plus plere 'to fill', so it names the un-filling of a container.
senses.whyCN: depletion 来自 de-「完全」加 plere「装满」，因此命名的是容器被卸空。

senses.title: Water tables falling
senses.definition: the lowering of groundwater because pumping removes water faster than rain replaces it
senses.definitionCN: 抽水快于降雨补给导致地下水位下降
senses.example: Farm pumping caused severe groundwater depletion.
senses.exampleCN: 农业抽水造成严重的地下水耗竭。
senses.why: an aquifer is a slow-filling container, so any pumping is literally depletion.
senses.whyCN: 含水层是一个装得很慢的容器，因此任何抽水都是字面上的 depletion。

senses.title: Thinning of the ozone layer
senses.definition: the loss of ozone molecules in the stratosphere, measured in concentration
senses.definitionCN: 平流层中臭氧分子的减少，以浓度计量
senses.example: Chlorofluorocarbons were blamed for ozone depletion.
senses.exampleCN: 氯氟烃被归咎为臭氧层损耗的原因。
senses.why: the same word works for an atmospheric layer because a layer is also a stock that can be thinned.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词也适用于大气层，因为一层气体同样是可被削薄的存量。

senses.title: Fish and timber overharvested
senses.titleCN: 鱼类与木材被过度采获
senses.definition: the decline of a renewable stock when harvest outruns regrowth
senses.definitionCN: 采获超过再生量时可再生存量的下降
senses.example: The bay suffered depletion of its shellfish beds.
senses.exampleCN: 这片海湾的贝类床遭受耗竭。
senses.why: a renewable stock is still a stock, so the word applies whenever the take exceeds the return.
senses.whyCN: 可再生资源仍是存量，因此只要取用超过回补，这个词就适用。

senses.title: Finite reserves running out
senses.definition: the one-way reduction of coal, oil or ore that cannot be replaced
senses.definitionCN: 煤、石油或矿石无法补充的单向减少
senses.example: The field reached depletion after forty years of drilling.
senses.exampleCN: 这块油田在钻采四十年后走向枯竭。
senses.why: with no refill, depletion is not a cycle but a countdown to zero.
senses.whyCN: 没有补充时，耗竭不是循环，而是倒数到零。

senses.title: Emptying the body in old medicine
senses.definition: the historical medical sense of removing blood or fluid to restore balance
senses.definitionCN: 历史上通过放血或排液恢复平衡的医学含义
senses.example: Early physicians prescribed depletion for fever.
senses.exampleCN: 早期医生为发热开出排空疗法。
senses.why: the word's first English use was medical, since the body too was imagined as a container to be emptied.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最早的英语用法是医学的，因为身体也被想象成可被倒空的容器。

senses.title: Natural capital written down
senses.definition: the drop in the recorded value of natural assets in national accounting
senses.definitionCN: 国民核算中自然资源资产记录价值的下降
senses.example: The audit separated depletion from ordinary depreciation.
senses.exampleCN: 审计把资源耗竭与普通折旧分开。
senses.why: economists use depletion for the using-up of a natural asset, just as accountants use depreciation for machines.
senses.whyCN: 经济学家用 depletion 指自然资产被用掉，正如会计用 depreciation 指机器折旧。

senses.title: Exhaustion of patience or energy
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：耐心或精力的耗尽
senses.definition: the running down of any personal or shared reserve such as energy, patience or trust
senses.definitionCN: 任何个人或共享储备的下降，如精力、耐心或信任
senses.example: The long shift produced a visible depletion of morale.
senses.exampleCN: 长班次造成了明显可见的士气耗减。
senses.why: the metaphor keeps the container shape, so anything that can be used up can be said to undergo depletion.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻保留容器形态，因此任何能被用光的东西都可以说经历 depletion。

intro.en: Depletion comes from Latin deplere 'to empty out', built on de- 'completely' and plere 'to fill'. It entered English first as a medical term. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: depletion 来自拉丁 deplere「倒空」，由 de-「完全」与 plere「装满」构成。它最初以医学术语进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Plere meant 'to fill'. It is the source of complete, supplement, replete and plenty's wider family.
items.cn: plere 意为「装满」。它是 complete、supplement、replete 以及 plenty 更广词族的来源。

items.en: De- 'completely' plus plere produced deplere 'to empty out, drain', the direct ancestor of the English noun.
items.cn: de-「完全」加 plere 构成 deplere「倒空、排干」，是英语名词的直接祖先。

items.en: The action noun depletio 'an emptying' supplied the shape of the English word.
items.cn: 动作名词 depletio「排空」提供了英语词的形态。

items.en: In seventeenth-century medicine depletion named the removal of blood or humours to restore balance.
items.cn: 在 17 世纪医学中，depletion 指放血或排液以恢复平衡。

items.en: By the nineteenth century the word had spread to any stock being used up, from mines to soil fertility.
items.cn: 到 19 世纪，这个词已扩展到任何被用掉的存量，从矿藏到土壤肥力。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the exact first use of the general non-medical sense is not recorded and cannot be tied to a single text.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：非医学的通用义最早出现在哪里没有记录，无法归到某一文本。

note.en: Group one holds forms of the same plere family that are often mixed up; group two holds words for a supply falling low.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 plere 词族、常被混用的形式；第二组是描述供给走低的词。

entries.definition: The verb for emptying a stock; depletion is the process or result noun built on it.
entries.definitionCN: 表示倒空存量的动词；depletion 是由它构成的过程或结果名词。

entries.definition: The participle used as an adjective for a stock already emptied, as in depleted soil.
entries.definitionCN: 作形容词的分词，指已被掏空的存量，如贫瘠化的土壤。

entries.definition: Re- 'again' plus plere 'fill': the state of being filled again, the mirror image of depletion.
entries.definitionCN: re-「再次」加 plere「装满」：再次充满的状态，是 depletion 的镜像。

entries.definition: Com- 'thoroughly' plus plere: filled to the end, hence finished; it shares the root but not the emptying direction.
entries.definitionCN: com-「彻底」加 plere：填到底，因而完成；共享词根，但方向不是倒空。

entries.definition: The state of having nothing left; depletion also covers partial reductions before that end.
entries.definitionCN: 什么都不剩的状态；depletion 也涵盖到达终点前的部分减少。

entries.definition: Insufficiency relative to demand; depletion is the physical drawing down that can cause it.
entries.definitionCN: 相对需求而言的不足；depletion 是可能造成它的物理性减少。

entries.definition: A measured fall in a stored supply such as an aquifer; it is a reading, while depletion is the wider process.
entries.definitionCN: 储存供给测得的下降，如含水层；它是一个读数，而 depletion 是更宽的过程。

entries.definition: The act of using goods or resources; consumption may be sustainable, whereas depletion implies the stock cannot keep up.
entries.definitionCN: 使用商品或资源的行为；消费可以是可持续的，而 depletion 暗示存量跟不上。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: de- 'completely' + plere 'fill': depletion is the un-filling of a container.
normal.cn: de-「完全」+ plere「装满」：depletion 就是容器被卸空。

normal.en: The opposite is repletion, built with re- 'again' on the same root.
normal.cn: 反义词是 repletion，用同一词根加 re-「再次」构成。

normal.en: The family runs deplete, depletion, depleted, replete, replenish, complete.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 deplete、depletion、depleted、replete、replenish、complete。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the fields: groundwater depletion, ozone depletion, resource depletion.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：地下水耗竭、臭氧层损耗、资源枯竭。

normal.en: Medicine used the word first: doctors depleted the body to restore balance.
normal.cn: 医学最早使用这个词：医生通过排空身体来恢复平衡。

abstract.en: Picture a cup that shows every sip it has ever lost.
abstract.cn: 想象一只杯子，把每一次被喝掉的量都显示出来。

abstract.en: Picture a battery whose bars disappear one by one.
abstract.cn: 想象一块电池，格子一格一格地消失。

abstract.en: Picture a reservoir wall wearing rings like a tree's age lines.
abstract.cn: 想象水库的墙长着年轮一样的圈。

examples.en: Ozone depletion peaked over Antarctica in spring.
examples.cn: 臭氧层损耗在南极上空于春季达到高峰。

examples.en: Depletion of the aquifer has lowered the whole valley.
examples.cn: 含水层的耗竭使整个河谷下沉。

examples.en: The report links soil depletion to falling yields.
examples.cn: 报告把土壤耗竭与产量下降联系起来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「de（向下）+ pletion（填满）」——把填满的东西往下卸空 → 耗竭

root: 拉丁 deplere「倒空」= de-「完全」+ plere「装满」；动作名词 depletio。plere 同族另有 complete、replete、supplement、replenish。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one container: a stock is full, something withdraws from it, the level falls, and the same noun then names water tables, an ozone layer, fish, ore, an old medical practice, a national account and finally a personal reserve.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一个容器展开：存量是满的、有东西被取走、水位下降，随后同一名词用来命名地下水位、臭氧层、鱼类、矿石、旧医学疗法、国民账户，最后指个人储备。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: rings of old water levels left on the wall of a drying reservoir.
core.cn: 核心意象：干涸水库的墙上留下一圈圈旧水位线。

branches.en: GENERAL AND MEDICAL: any container can be emptied, whether a reservoir or a body treated by old medicine.
branches.cn: 通用与医学：任何容器都可被倒空，无论是水库还是旧医学处理的身体。

branches.en: WATER AND AIR: aquifers and the ozone layer are both slow-filling stocks measured by level or concentration.
branches.cn: 水与空气：含水层与臭氧层都是补充缓慢的存量，按水位或浓度计量。

branches.en: HARVEST AND RESERVE: renewable stocks can still be overharvested, and finite reserves simply count down.
branches.cn: 采获与储量：可再生存量仍会被过度采获，有限储量则只是倒数。

branches.en: ACCOUNTING: treasuries record the using-up of natural assets as a loss.
branches.cn: 核算：财政部门把自然资产被用掉记为损失。

branches.en: PERSONAL RESERVE: energy, patience and trust behave like stocks once withdrawals outrun recovery.
branches.cn: 个人储备：一旦抽取超过恢复，精力、耐心与信任就像存量一样。

intro.en: Depletion is a Latin action noun: a prefix of completion, a verb of filling, and a suffix of result. The same three pieces build a large English family.
intro.cn: depletion 是一个拉丁动作名词：表示「完全」的前缀、表示「装满」的动词、表示结果的后缀。同三块构件构成一个庞大的英语词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin deplere and depletio give deplete and depletion; plere also gives complete, replete, supplement and replenish.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 deplere 与 depletio 衍生 deplete 与 depletion；plere 还衍生 complete、replete、supplement 与 replenish。

definition_en: to move troops or resources into position for action, or to use something effectively
core_image: 指挥图上箭头把几支队伍调到不同位置，服务器机房里新版本被推上线
scene: 公司部署了新的服务器。The company deployed new servers.
sceneCN: 第 2 个义项：deployed 指有效利用、投入使用；句意是公司部署了新的服务器。

pos.zh: 部署；调动；有效利用；（计算机）部署，发布

senses.title: Position troops
senses.definition: to move soldiers or equipment into position for action
senses.definitionCN: 把士兵或装备调到可行动的位置
senses.example: The army deployed two brigades along the border.
senses.exampleCN: 军队沿边境部署了两个旅。
senses.why: Arrows on a map moving units into place.
senses.whyCN: 地图上一支支部队被箭头调到位置。

senses.title: Use effectively
senses.definition: to bring resources or skills into effective use
senses.definitionCN: 把资源或技能投入有效使用
senses.example: The company deployed new servers.
senses.exampleCN: 公司部署了新的服务器。
senses.why: A budget line moved to where it works hardest.
senses.whyCN: 一笔预算被挪到最能起作用的地方。

senses.title: Release software
senses.definition: to put a program or system into service on a server
senses.definitionCN: 把程序或系统放到服务器上投入使用
senses.example: They deploy the update every Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 他们每周五发布更新。
senses.why: A green light beside a version number.
senses.whyCN: 一个版本号旁边亮起的绿灯。

intro.en: Deploy comes from French déployer, from Latin displicare, dis- plus plicare, to fold: to unfold.
intro.cn: deploy 源自法语 déployer，来自拉丁语 displicare，由 dis- 加 plicare（折叠）构成：展开。

items.en: Plicare meant to fold.
items.cn: plicare 意为折叠。

items.en: Displicare meant to unfold or spread out.
items.cn: displicare 意为展开、铺开。

items.en: Déployer meant to spread out troops.
items.cn: 法语 déployer 指把部队展开。

items.en: Deploy entered English for spreading forces.
items.cn: 十八世纪 deploy 以展开兵力义进入英语。

items.en: It widened to using resources effectively.
items.cn: 二十世纪扩展到有效利用资源。

items.en: Deploy became the word for releasing software.
items.cn: 二十一世纪 deploy 成为发布软件的说法。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the ploy- folding family; the near-meaning group names other ways of putting things in place.
note.cn: 形近组共享 ploy-（折叠）家族；近义组是其他「就位」的说法。

entries.definition: The act of deploying troops or software.
To spread out for people to see.
To use something, or give someone work.
To put something in a particular place.
To put someone in a place for duty.
To make something available for use.

normalIntro.en: Deploy is de- out plus ploy- fold: unfold what was folded and put it where it works.
normalIntro.cn: deploy 就是 de-（向外）加 ploy-（折叠）：把折起来的展开，放到能起作用的位置。

normal.en: Ploy- means to fold, as in employ.
normal.cn: ploy- 意为折叠，如 employ。

normal.en: De- here means out.
normal.cn: 这里 de- 表示向外。

normal.en: Deploy troops means spread them out.
normal.cn: deploy troops 指把部队展开。

normal.en: Deploy resources means put them to work.
normal.cn: deploy resources 指把资源投入使用。

normal.en: Deploy the update means put it live.
normal.cn: deploy the update 指把更新上线。

abstract.en: Arrows on a map moving units into place.
abstract.cn: 地图上一支支部队被箭头调到位置。

abstract.en: A budget line moved to where it works hardest.
abstract.cn: 一笔预算被挪到最能起作用的地方。

abstract.en: A green light beside a version number.
abstract.cn: 一个版本号旁边亮起的绿灯。

examples.en: The team deployed the fix overnight.
examples.cn: 团队连夜部署了修复。

examples.en: They are deploying sensors across the valley.
examples.cn: 他们正在整个山谷布置传感器。

examples.en: She deploys her skills where they matter most.
examples.cn: 她把技能用在最要紧的地方。

dict_mnemonic.text: deploy 谐音「弟普洛伊」——不如记 de（展开）＋ ploy（折，与 display 同根 plicare）＝把折起来的铺开，「部署、展开」，软件里就是「发布上线」。

root: 拉丁语 plicare（折叠）→ displicare（展开）→ 法语 déployer → 英语 deploy（部署）

sensesIntro.en: One unfolding: troops on a map, a budget line and a version number.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一次展开：地图上的部队、一笔预算与一个版本号。

branches.en: Arrows on a map moving units into place.

definition_en: to put money into a bank or account, money paid as a first part, or material laid down by water
core_image: 一枚硬币落进铁盒，盒底已经有薄薄一层
scene: 房东数完钱，把一张收据推过来，说钥匙可以拿了。She deposited the money and kept the receipt.
sceneCN: 这里 deposit 指「存入」（第 1 个义项：把钱放进银行或账户）；句意是她把钱存进去并保留了收据。

senses.title: Put money in for keeping
senses.definition: to put money into a bank or an account
senses.definitionCN: 把钱放进银行或账户
senses.example: She deposited the money and kept the receipt.
senses.exampleCN: 她把钱存进去并保留了收据。
senses.why: Money put down in a safe place is money set apart from the pocket.
senses.whyCN: 放进安全地方的钱，就是与口袋分开的钱。

senses.title: Money paid as a first part
senses.definition: money paid first as a promise or a security
senses.definitionCN: 先付的一笔作为承诺或担保的钱
senses.example: They paid a deposit on the flat.
senses.exampleCN: 他们为这套公寓付了押金。
senses.why: A deposit says the promise has weight.
senses.whyCN: 押金是在说，这个承诺有分量。

senses.title: Material laid down by water
senses.definition: material that water or wind leaves in a layer
senses.definitionCN: 水或风留下的一层物质
senses.example: The river left a deposit of sand at the bend.
senses.exampleCN: 河流在转弯处留下一层沙。
senses.why: Water carries what it cannot hold, and sets it down.
senses.whyCN: 水搬不动的东西，就放下来。

intro.en: Deposit comes from Latin depositum, a thing placed down, from deponere, built on ponere, to place.
intro.cn: deposit 来自拉丁语 depositum（放下之物），源头是 deponere，词基为 ponere（放置）。

items.en: Deponere joined de-, meaning down, with ponere, to place.
items.cn: deponere 由 de-（向下）与 ponere（放置）合成。

items.en: Depositum named a thing placed down or entrusted.
items.cn: depositum 指放下或托付之物。

items.en: English used deposit for money placed with a bank.
items.cn: 英语用 deposit 指存进银行的钱。

items.en: Science borrowed it for layers laid down by water.
items.cn: 科学借它指水留下的层状物。

items.en: Now it covers savings, security payments and sediment.
items.cn: 如今它覆盖储蓄、担保付款与沉积物。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the deposit stem, and the meaning group moves from saving money to leaving matter behind.
note.cn: 形近组共用 deposit 词干，近义组则从存钱走到留下物质。

normal.en: A deposit is money told to sit down and wait.
normal.cn: 存款就是让钱坐下来等着。

normal.en: A deposit on a flat is a promise with a price.

normal.en: A river deposits what it is too tired to carry.

abstract.cn: 想象一只手把硬币投进投币口。

abstract.en: Picture a receipt folded once and put in a pocket.
abstract.cn: 想象一张收据被折一下，塞进口袋。

abstract.en: Picture a thin line of sand along a river bend.
abstract.cn: 想象河湾边上薄薄的一道沙。
